question: How much revenue do missed calls cost Punctual Pros?
html:
What missed calls cost Punctual Pros

Missed calls cost Punctual Pros about $1.4M a year in recoverable revenue (est.), roughly 6% of its estimated ~$22M revenue (Voice AI research). This is a model figure. The company's actual call logs are not in the context.

How the estimate works

  • Monthly inbound calls are about 3,502 (est.). They are backed out of the ~$22M revenue estimate, a 70% call-driven share, and a $1,024 average ticket (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings).
  • About 14.8% of calls go unanswered (est.). The model weights a 12% after-hours share losing 35% and an 88% daytime share losing 12%.
  • AI recovers 80% of those calls and books 45% of them. A 40% haircut covers callers who would have called back.
  • The result is about 1,343 incremental jobs a year at $1,024 each.
ComponentAnnual revenue (est.)
After-hours missed calls$390,000
Daytime and storm overflow$982,000
Recoverable from missed calls$1,372,000
Outbound membership renewal (separate lever)$403,000
Total voice AI opportunity$1,775,000 (8.1% of revenue)

Why the range is wide

  • The model allows a missed-call share between 10% and 35%. At Invoca's industry-level 35% miss rate, the recoverable figure scales to about $3.2M (est.) (Voice AI research).
  • The model is built on a revenue base that is itself an estimate. FY2025 pro forma revenue is ~$22M, with a range of $16-28M (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Vendor booking rates are self-reported and unaudited. ServiceTitan reports a 70% AI booking rate against a 42% typical human rate.
  • Leaks cluster at demand peaks. Off-hours calls were 14.1% of HVAC inbound in June versus 9.8% in October (Punctual Pros demand model). Losses are likely concentrated in summer heat and storm days (est.).
  • The gross value of all missed calls is larger than $1.4M. That figure would need real missed-call counts and the true callback rate.

Data that would firm this up

  • ServiceTitan or phone-system logs covering inbound volume, abandoned calls, and answer rate by hour and day.
  • Booking rate by customer service rep and by time slot.
  • Membership count and renewal rate. The 6,000-member figure is an assumption.
  • Daily booked calls by trade, to calibrate the demand model's weather multipliers.

Next actions

  1. Pull 12 months of call and booking data from Punctual Pros' ServiceTitan instance. Replace the modelled 14.8% miss rate with actuals.
  2. Split missed calls by hour, trade and weather day. Size after-hours and storm overflow separately.
  3. Load the history into the demand model to fit the weather elasticities and set county market share.
  4. Scope a 90-day after-hours AI answering pilot with a measured control period. Track booked jobs, not vendor-reported deflection.

# What missed calls cost Punctual Pros

Missed calls cost Punctual Pros about **$1.4M a year in recoverable revenue (est.)**, roughly 6% of its estimated ~$22M revenue (Voice AI research). This is a model figure. The company's actual call logs are not in the context.

## How the estimate works

- Monthly inbound calls are about 3,502 (est.). They are backed out of the ~$22M revenue estimate, a 70% call-driven share, and a $1,024 average ticket (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings).
- About 14.8% of calls go unanswered (est.). The model weights a 12% after-hours share losing 35% and an 88% daytime share losing 12%.
- AI recovers 80% of those calls and books 45% of them. A 40% haircut covers callers who would have called back.
- The result is about 1,343 incremental jobs a year at $1,024 each.

| Component | Annual revenue (est.) |
|---|---|
| After-hours missed calls | $390,000 |
| Daytime and storm overflow | $982,000 |
| **Recoverable from missed calls** | **$1,372,000** |
| Outbound membership renewal (separate lever) | $403,000 |
| Total voice AI opportunity | $1,775,000 (8.1% of revenue) |

## Why the range is wide

- The model allows a missed-call share between 10% and 35%. At Invoca's industry-level 35% miss rate, the recoverable figure scales to about $3.2M (est.) (Voice AI research).
- The model is built on a revenue base that is itself an estimate. FY2025 pro forma revenue is ~$22M, with a range of $16-28M (Punctual Pros public filings).
- Vendor booking rates are self-reported and unaudited. ServiceTitan reports a 70% AI booking rate against a 42% typical human rate.
- Leaks cluster at demand peaks. Off-hours calls were 14.1% of HVAC inbound in June versus 9.8% in October (Punctual Pros demand model). Losses are likely concentrated in summer heat and storm days (est.).
- The gross value of all missed calls is larger than $1.4M. That figure would need real missed-call counts and the true callback rate.

## Data that would firm this up

- ServiceTitan or phone-system logs covering inbound volume, abandoned calls, and answer rate by hour and day.
- Booking rate by customer service rep and by time slot.
- Membership count and renewal rate. The 6,000-member figure is an assumption.
- Daily booked calls by trade, to calibrate the demand model's weather multipliers.

## Next actions

1. Pull 12 months of call and booking data from Punctual Pros' ServiceTitan instance. Replace the modelled 14.8% miss rate with actuals.
2. Split missed calls by hour, trade and weather day. Size after-hours and storm overflow separately.
3. Load the history into the demand model to fit the weather elasticities and set county market share.
4. Scope a 90-day after-hours AI answering pilot with a measured control period. Track booked jobs, not vendor-reported deflection.
